title: Uniform provisions concerning the protection of motor vehicles against unauthorized use (Devices to prevent unauthorized use), version 0.5.0
scope_summary: Approves vehicles of categories M1 and N1 with regard to their devices to prevent unauthorized use, i.e. a locking system preventing normal engine/main power activation combined with a steering, transmission, gearshift or brake lock; components and devices may also be approved. Fitting to other vehicle categories is optional, but any device fitted must comply, and approvals for other categories and their devices may be granted on manufacturer request.
scope_quote: 1.1 Approval of a vehicle of category M1 and N1 with regard to its devices to prevent unauthorized use. 1.2 The fitting of devices to vehicles of other categories is optional but any such device fitted is required to comply with all relevant provisions of this Regulation. 1.3 At the request of the manufacturer, Contracting Parties may grant approvals according to this Regulation to vehicles of other categories and devices for fitment to such vehicles. 1.4 This Regulation does not apply to radio transmission frequencies, whether or not related to the protection of vehicles against unauthorized use.
vehicle_categories: other categories optionally (on manufacturer request, par. 1.2/1.3)
applies_to_components: Device to prevent unauthorized use (locking system)
Steering lock (steering control, steering column, cladding, steering shaft, steering gearbox)
Electrical/electronic components of the locking system
relation_to_other_regulations: Vehicle categories M1/N1 as defined in the Consolidated Resolution R.E.3 (ECE/TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.6); approval mark country codes per R.E.3 Annex 3
Par. 4.5 allows the approval mark to be combined with approvals under other UN Regulations
Not stated in the provided text, but R161 is part of the split of UN R116: R161 covers devices to prevent unauthorized use, while immobilizers and vehicle alarm systems are covered by R162 and R163
Annex 7 EMC tests (immunity to conducted, radiated and ESD disturbances, plus radiated emissions) refer to external technical prescriptions, presumably ISO standards and/or UN R10
Annex 9 (digital key) requires robustness against cyber-attacks, which has a likely interface with UN R155 cyber security (not stated in the provided text)
Radio transmission frequencies are excluded from scope (par. 1.4); these are left to radio regulations

defined_terms.definition: A device subject to the requirements of this Regulation and intended to be part of a vehicle, which may be type-approved independently of a vehicle where the Regulation expressly provides.
A device subject to this Regulation and intended to be part of a vehicle, which may be type-approved separately but only in relation to one or more specified vehicle types.
Motor vehicles not differing in the manufacturer's type designation, the arrangement and design of the components on which the device acts, or the type of device to prevent unauthorized use.

A locking system designed to prevent unauthorized normal activation of the engine or other main power source, combined with at least one system that locks the steering, transmission, gearshift control or brakes (a brake lock must not automatically release the brakes against the driver's intention on deactivation).
The steering control, steering column and its cladding, steering shaft, steering gearbox and all other components directly affecting the effectiveness of the device.
One of the specifically developed variations of a locking system which, when properly activated, permits operation of the locking system.
Any mechanical and/or electronic solution designed to provide a method of operating a locking system designed to be operated by it.
An electronic code of several elements whose combination changes at random after each operation of the transmitting unit.
A user able to authorize digital keys, of whom there may be more than one.
A key designed to be transferred to multiple devices by the primary user(s) through dedicated processes.
A distance of less than 6 m.

applicability_hints: Any steering column lock, electronic steering lock (ESL), transmission park lock, gearshift lock or brake-based lock that, combined with engine/power activation blocking, prevents vehicle use falls under this Regulation
Applies to electric and hybrid vehicles too: 'engine or other source of main engine power' covers propulsion system activation (start/ready mode)
Ignition switches/start-stop buttons, keyless entry/start systems, key fobs and transponder keys are 'keys' (mechanical and/or electronic) and their locking system is covered
Smartphone/wearable-based digital keys shared by a primary user are covered by Annex 9, including cyber-attack robustness and 'close proximity' (<6 m) requirements
Electronic components of the locking system must pass Annex 6 operation tests (voltage, temperature, vibration) and Annex 7 EMC tests; some components are exempt from Annex 6 (see Annex 6 par. 1)
Steering components (wheel, column, cladding, shaft, gearbox) that directly affect lock effectiveness are part of 'steering' and therefore relevant to approval and type definition
Changing the steering column design or the type of locking device creates a new vehicle type (par. 2.4)
Non-M1/N1 vehicles (e.g. M2, N2, L) are not required to fit such devices, but if they do, the devices must comply (par. 1.2)
Radio transmission frequencies of remote keys are outside scope (par. 1.4), although remote key electronics remain subject to the EMC and other requirements
Immobilizers and vehicle alarm systems are not covered here; they fall under the split-off sister regulations (R162/R163, formerly R116)
